notes: Central Standard Swedish. COMPLEMENTARY QUANTITY: in a stressed syllable a long vowel is followed by a short consonant and a short vowel by a long consonant or a cluster (Riad 2014; Wikipedia: 'a phonologically short consonant follows a long vowel and a long consonant follows a short vowel'). Encoded with data only: doubled consonant letters are grapheme keys mapping to /Cː/ (⟨ck⟩→/kː/), consonant clusters are grapheme keys mapping to the concatenated phonemes, the stressed nucleus takes the long vowel via `positional_graphemes.nucleus_stressed`, and allophone rules shorten it again when the next phoneme is one of those long/cluster phonemes. SOFTENING: ⟨k g sk⟩ → [ɕ j ɧ] before a front vowel (e i y ä ö) — expressed with the BEFORE_FRONT_VOWEL class, so ⟨å⟩ (axis-ambiguous) correctly keeps the hard reading. RETROFLEXION: /r/ + a following dental coronal fuses into one retroflex — rt→[ʈ] rd→[ɖ] rn→[ɳ] rs→[ʂ] rl→[ɭ], with the /r/ absorbed (Riad 2014 ch. 4; Engstrand 1999 p. 141). Implemented as SV_RETROFLEX_* allophone rules; a previous revision dropped it from base sv because it costs PER against the wikipron gold, which spells the cluster out in 390 of 580 r+coronal rows — but the higher-tier lexicon-derived gold (Folkets lexikon, KTH, via ipa-dict; n=21095) retroflexes systematically (barn /bɑːɳ/, bord /buːɖ/, kort /kɔʈː/, fars /faʂː/, pärla /²pɛːɭa/), and o2i's own sv-FI / sv-x-rikssvenska / sv-x-skanska descendants already retroflex, so base sv was the outlier. PRE-R LOWERING: ⟨ä⟩/⟨ö⟩ lower to [æ(ː)]/[œ(ː)] before /r/ and the retroflexes. NO FINAL DEVOICING: Swedish keeps final /b d ɡ/ (the previous spec devoiced them — that was wrong). TONE: accent 1/2 is lexical and is not encoded; the gold marks it (¹/²), which is a convention difference.

stress.notes: Germanic initial stress (Riad 2014). Pitch accent: accent 2 (grave, marked ²) for penult-stressed words in final ⟨-a⟩/⟨-e⟩ — the disyllabic-trochee core class (Riad 2014, ch. 10: accent 2 requires a post-stress syllable; infinitives and weak nouns in -a/-e carry it by default, antepenult-stressed words keep accent 1). Accent 1 left unmarked, matching the wikipron convention.

allophone_rules.notes: Pre-r lowering under stress (Riad 2014, §3.3): a stressed front mid vowel lowers to [æ] before /r/ — long before a single r (lära [læːra], är [æːr]), short-and-lowered when the r heads a cluster or is itself long (ärt [æʈ/ært], Bert, berg, herr). Unstressed ⟨-er⟩ keeps [ɛr] (vinter), hence the stress gate.

Retroflex assimilation (Riad 2014, ch. 4; Engstrand 1999 p.141): /r/ plus a following dental coronal fuses into a single retroflex — rt->[ʈ], rd->[ɖ], rn->[ɳ], rs->[ʂ], rl->[ɭ] (kort [kɔʈː], bord [buːɖ], barn [bɑːɳ], fars [faʂː], pärla [pɛːɭa]). The /r/ does not surface separately. A GEMINATE ⟨rr⟩ does not feed it: the KTH lexicon keeps [rː] plus a plain coronal in 10 of its 11 ⟨rr⟩+coronal entries (Norrland /nɔrːland/, borrning /bɔrːnɪŋ/, spärrlinje /spɛrːlɪnːjɛ/), so only a single /r/ triggers.

Retroflex assimilation spreads through the whole coronal cluster (Riad 2014 ch. 4; Elert 1970): in ⟨rst⟩ ⟨rns⟩ ⟨rts⟩ the dental AFTER the first one is retroflex too, not just the first — första [fœʂʈa], värst [væʂʈ], barnsben [bɑːɳʂbeːn], blyerts [blyːɛʈʂ], bortse [bɔʈʂeː]. /s/ cascades like the stops, so the set is t d n s l. The condition reaches exactly two slots back to the /r/, so it covers r+C+C but not a third link: världsdel is [vɛːɖʂdeːl] in the lexicon and the rules give [væɭɖsdɛl], which is a known and accepted limit of this encoding, not a claim about Swedish. Conditioned on the underlying /r/ two slots back, so a coronal cluster with no /r/ (kista, storm) is untouched.
